_comment: GBIF vernacular names are global, not North American. Mostly it gets US names right -- of 38 spot-checked common Massachusetts species only Circus cyaneus was outright wrong. The rest are lumped slash-forms, and they cannot be resolved automatically: 'Great Blue/Cocoi Heron' needs the trailing noun, while 'Great Cormorant/European Shag' must keep its own. Same shape, opposite rule. So they are written out. Keyed by scientific name.
